subtitle_zh: Dean Kernott 独白：提出第四种避险，剖析美债信心危机与 AI 集中度，主张趁波动率便宜买入尾部保护。

turns.en: Hello, this is Dean Kernott, and welcome to the Alpha Exchange, where we explore topics in financial markets associated with managing risk, generating return, and the deployment of capital in the alternative investment industry.
turns.zh: 大家好，我是 Dean Kernott，欢迎收听 Alpha Exchange。在这个节目里，我们探讨金融市场的各类话题，涉及风险管理、收益创造，以及另类投资行业里的资本配置。

turns.en: Each year in early September, I make a point of heading to Lower Manhattan to walk around the site that was the original Twin Towers at the World Trade Center.
turns.zh: 每年九月初，我都会特意去一趟 Lower Manhattan，在 World Trade Center 原 Twin Towers 的遗址上走一走。

turns.en: I find great meaning in sitting quietly by the reflecting pool, letting my mind wander. For years, I commuted into the Trade Center, dutifully taking the one-in-nine subway, along with thousands of others, first during my time at Nemora in the early 1990s and then at Lehman in the late 90s.
turns.zh: 坐在纪念池边静静待一会儿，任思绪游走，这对我意义非凡。好多年里我都通勤去 World Trade Center 上班，和成千上万人一样老老实实坐 1 号线转 9 号线的地铁，先是在 90 年代初供职 Nemora 那会儿，然后是 90 年代末在 Lehman。

turns.en: I was at B of A in Midtown on September 11, 2001. It's hard to believe it's been 25 years, but here we are. The 9-Eleven Memorial Museum is a powerful, solemn place to visit.
turns.zh: 2001 年 9 月 11 日那天，我在 Midtown 的 B of A。很难相信已经过去 25 年了，但事实如此。9/11 纪念博物馆是一个震撼人心、庄严肃穆的地方。

turns.en: I recommend it. Here's a statement from the website. Quote, A quarter century after the September 11, 2001 attacks, 100 million Americans are too young to remember that day that changed our city and nation forever.
turns.zh: 我很推荐大家去看看。官网上有段话，我念一下：“2001 年 9 月 11 日袭击事件过去四分之一个世纪，仍有 1 亿美国人因为太年轻，不记得那个永远改变了我们城市和国家的日子。”

turns.en: It is our shared promise, made 25 years ago, to never forget, so those born after 9-Eleven learn its significance in enduring legacy. As we commemorate this anniversary, a new generation will learn about the unimaginable loss we experienced and the inspiring stories of bravery, compassion, unity, and service that we witnessed and have rippled through the decades.
turns.zh: 这是我们 25 年前共同许下的承诺：永不遗忘，让 9/11 之后出生的人明白它的意义与长存的遗产。在这个纪念周年来临之际，新一代将了解到我们曾经历的难以想象的创伤，也将了解我们亲眼见证、并在数十年来不断传递的那些关于勇气、悲悯、团结与奉献的故事。

turns.en: George Bush's approval rating reached 90% in the weeks following 9-Eleven. I'll not forget the first pitch he threw out at Game 3 of the 2001 World Series at Yankee Stadium.
turns.zh: 9/11 之后的几个星期里，George Bush 的支持率冲到了 90%。我不会忘记他在 Yankee Stadium 的 2001 年 World Series 第三场上投出的开球第一球。

turns.en: He looked as confident as ever, walking out in an FTNY jacket. He pipes in a gorgeous strike. What a moment. I'm hoping that 9-Eleven, 2026, provides some opportunity for us all to reflect on such a consequential day in our country's history.
turns.zh: 他穿着一件 FTNY 夹克走出来，看上去一如既往地自信，结果还投出了一个漂亮的好球。那真是历史性的一刻。我希望 2026 年的 9/11 能给我们所有人一个机会，去反思这个在我国历史上如此重大的日子。

turns.en: The stock market never opened on Tuesday, 9-Eleven, 2001, nor did it open for the remaining days of the week. When it did, on 9-17, the S&P fell by 4.9%.
turns.zh: 2001 年 9 月 11 日周二，股市当天没有开盘，那一周剩下的几天也都没开。等到 9 月 17 日重新开盘，S&P 下跌了 4.9%。

turns.en: The VIX soared to 41.7%. The yield on the 10-year fell by 20 basis points from 9-10 to 9-17. The 2-year yield fell by 55 basis points. The Fed eased by 50 basis points on an emergency, inter-meeting basis.
turns.zh: VIX 飙升到 41.7%。从 9 月 10 日到 9 月 17 日，10 年期国债收益率下行 20 个基点，2 年期收益率下行 55 个基点。美联储在非例会的间隙紧急降息 50 个基点。

turns.en: Back then, the bond market was reliably a flight-to-safety asset. But as inflation has been consistently above target for more than 60 months, that has changed.
turns.zh: 在那时候，债市是妥妥的避险资产。但当通胀连续 60 多个月高于目标水平之后，这一点已经变了。

turns.en: And that change is the subject of the discussion that follows. Back in June, I wrote a piece called The Three Types of Risk Off. In July, I followed up with a podcast that detailed the work which provides a framework for thinking about risk events through the interaction between stock and bond prices.
turns.zh: 这个变化正是接下来要讨论的主题。今年 6 月，我写过一篇文章叫《The Three Types of Risk Off》（避险的三种类型）。7 月我又跟了一期播客，详细介绍了这项研究——它提供了一个通过股债价格互动来思考风险事件的框架。

turns.en: To very briefly summarize, there is the classic risk off, the taper, and the liquidation. In the classic, the equity market gets hit, and the treasury market rallies on a flight-to-safety.
turns.zh: 简要概括一下：有经典避险（classic risk off）、紧缩式避险（taper）和平仓式避险（liquidation）。在经典避险里，股市挨打，国债市场因避险资金涌入而上涨。

turns.en: Old school, post-GFC kind of price action. Stock and bond prices are negatively correlated in the classic risk off. In the taper, the bond market motivates the risk off.
turns.zh: 那是老派的、金融危机（GFC）之后的价格行为。经典避险中，股债价格负相关。而在 taper 式避险里，是债市主导了避险。

turns.en: Uncertainty around Fed policy and how high yields may ultimately go forces investors to reprice equities. Stock and bond prices fall together as they did in the original taper tantrum of 2013 and also during the 2022 tightening cycle.
turns.zh: 围绕美联储政策和收益率最终会走多高的不确定性，迫使投资者重新给股票定价。股债价格一起下跌，就像 2013 年最初的缩减恐慌（taper tantrum），以及 2022 年紧缩周期时那样。

turns.en: Risk and bonds are positively correlated in the taper. In the liquidation, the treasury market initially rallies on a flight-to-safety, but ultimately is subject to a violent unwind as well as investors need to convert assets to cash.
turns.zh: 在 taper 里，股票和债券正相关。在 liquidation 里，国债市场一开始因避险而上涨，但当投资者需要把资产换成现金时，它最终也逃不掉被猛烈抛售。

turns.en: Even risk-free duration exposure is liquidated. Here, stock and bond prices are initially negatively correlated, but that flips to positive in the extreme meltdown.
turns.zh: 连无风险的久期（duration）敞口都会被平仓。这种情况下，股债价格起初负相关，但在极端崩溃中反转为正相关。

turns.en: First 2020 is the last liquidation event. Hopefully, we won't see this again for a long time. These episodes are dangerous and require a kitchen sink response from policymakers.
turns.zh: 2020 年 3 月就是最近一次 liquidation 事件。希望很长时间里我们都不要再看到它。这类时刻非常危险，需要政策制定者掏出整个工具箱（kitchen sink）式的应对。

turns.en: As I offered concluding thoughts for that paper, I suggested that a fourth risk off might be possible as well. Let me read what I wrote. My Minsky and Soros-inspired framework for thinking about risk views market prices as not merely an outcome, but a cause.
turns.zh: 在那篇文章的结尾，我提出还可能存在第四种避险。我把当时写的念一下：我这套受 Minsky 和 Soros 启发的风险思考框架，把市场价格看作不仅是结果，更是原因。

turns.en: Prices do not just react to risk, they are a source of risk. In this context, we might think about a fourth classification of risk off. This would be a liquidation episode that actually starts with the treasury market.
turns.zh: 价格不只是对风险做出反应，价格本身就是风险的来源。在这个语境下，我们可以设想第四类避险：一场实际上由国债市场率先引爆的 liquidation。

turns.en: It is to be distinguished from the taper in its cause and severity. The taper risk off focuses on changes in monetary policy and the intentions of the Fed.
turns.zh: 它与 taper 的区别在于成因和烈度。taper 式避险关注的是货币政策变化和美联储的意图。

turns.en: It leads to higher rates in lower stock prices, but the credibility of the quote system of government debt remains well intact. In this fourth type of risk off, the system suffers a crisis of confidence.
turns.zh: 它会导致利率更高、股价更低，但政府债务体系的公信力依然完好无损。而在第四种避险里，体系遭遇了信心危机。

turns.en: There is a sharp decline in the willingness to hold U.S. government debt. It is a loss of confidence for any number of reasons, but the main factor is a belief that the debt level is too great, the governance too weak, and the agency costs too intractable to address it.
turns.zh: 持有美国国债的意愿急剧下降。信心的丧失可能有各种各样的原因，但主因是这样一种信念：债务规模太大、治理太弱、代理成本（agency costs）太顽固，无从解决。

turns.en: Here it is the U.S. tenure note, not the S&P, that is the risk asset. From a true contagion standpoint, the quote risk-free bond market is the vulnerability.
turns.zh: 在这里，10 年期美债——而不是 S&P——才是风险资产。从真正的传染（contagion）角度看，所谓“无风险”的债市才是那个薄弱环节。

turns.en: If that is ultimately judged to be the wrong price, then every asset linked to it will be repriced as well. And that is where I want to start this podcast discussion.
turns.zh: 如果它的定价最终被证明是错的，那么所有与它挂钩的资产都会被重新定价。这正是我想开始这期播客讨论的地方。

turns.en: Because for all the wrong reasons, the U.S. Treasury market has become front page news. As distinguished again from the taper, the fourth risk off doesn't have all that much to do with Fed policy.
turns.zh: 因为美国国债市场出于种种不该有的原因上了头版。再次强调，与 taper 不同，第四种避险同美联储政策的关系并不大。

turns.en: It's really not much about inflation either. It's driven by the clearing price for the back end of the bond market, which in turn is an outcome of supply and demand, and to a large extent, that's driven by credibility.
turns.zh: 它也真的不那么关乎通胀。它是由债市长端（back end）的清算价格驱动的，而长端价格是供求的结果，很大程度上又取决于公信力。

turns.en: I worry that an erosion of confidence among the buyer base can impinge demand and lead to a rapid and unwelcome price adjustment in the risk-free Treasury market.
turns.zh: 我担心，买家群体信心的侵蚀会损害需求，让这个“无风险”的国债市场出现快速而不受欢迎的价格调整。

turns.en: If that should happen, what is already attracting too much attention will become a market risk factor that dominates media narratives and impacts investor psyche.
turns.zh: 如果真的发生，这个已经在吸引过多注意的东西，会变成一个主导媒体叙事、冲击投资者心理的市场风险因素。

turns.en: As I've said in this circumstance, it is the 10-year note, not the S&P, that is the risk asset. I'm a big believer in the power of narratives.
turns.zh: 正如我说过的，在这种情形下，风险资产是 10 年期美债，而不是 S&P。我深信叙事（narratives）的力量。

turns.en: We all consume an enormous amount, way too much in fact, of content each day. We doom scroll on Twitter. Our phones are set up to instantly alert us of news developments, the latest hot take or opinion piece, the newest political battle taken up by our elected officials.
turns.zh: 我们每个人每天消费的内容都多到离谱——事实上实在太多了。我们在 Twitter 上无休止地刷着坏消息（doomscrolling）。手机被设定成即时提醒我们新闻进展、最新的 hot take 或评论文章、民选官员们最新开打的骂战。

turns.en: Ordering a coffee, check your phone while you wait. On the train, good time for an Instagram scroll. In a cab, on your phone. At a game, check your phone.
turns.zh: 点咖啡的时候，等一杯的工夫刷一下手机。在地铁上，正好刷一波 Instagram。在出租车上，人在手机上。看球赛，也在看手机。

turns.en: Elevators, waiting rooms, airports, before bed, when you wake up. Check, check, check. The phone is everywhere. The conventional telling is that the iPhone arrived in 2007 and attention collapsed into it.
turns.zh: 电梯里、候诊时、机场、睡前、刚醒，刷、刷、刷。手机无处不在。通常的说法是：iPhone 2007 年问世，注意力就此坍缩进了它。

turns.en: The data does not support that. For the first four to five years, the smartphone was a utility. Maps, email, weather. eMarketer put average US adult non-voice mobile time at 46 minutes a day in 2011, under an hour.
turns.zh: 数据并不支持这个说法。头四五年里，智能手机只是一个工具：地图、邮件、天气。eMarketer 的数据显示，2011 年美国成人每天平均非通话移动时间只有 46 分钟，不到一小时。

turns.en: Five years later, after the device shipped, the phone was a hardware story with no attention story attached to it. Time spent on it barely moved.
turns.zh: 设备上市五年之后，手机讲的仍是一个硬件的故事，并没有附带什么注意力的故事，花在它上面的时间几乎没动。

turns.en: The step function came later and it wasn't the phone, but the apps built on top of it. In its February 2012 S1, Facebook disclosed that 425 million people were reaching it monthly from a phone, while flagging as a risk factor that mobile usage generated essentially no revenue and that continued migration from PCs to phones could hurt results.
turns.zh: 阶跃式的拐点来得更晚，而且不在手机本身，在于手机上生长出来的应用。Facebook 在 2012 年 2 月的 S-1 文件里披露，每月有 4.25 亿人用手机访问它，同时把一条风险因素摆在那里：移动端的使用几乎不产生收入，而用户从 PC 向手机的持续迁移可能拖累业绩。

turns.en: The mobile app had no ads in it. The stock lost roughly half its value within three months of the IPO as the market took that warning seriously.
turns.zh: 手机 App 里一条广告都没有。市场当真了这个警告，股价在 IPO 后三个月内跌去了大约一半。

turns.en: In 2012, mobile ads constituted 14% of Facebook ad revenue. By 2018, it was 92%. The time series in terms of time spent on the phone moved in lockstep.
turns.zh: 2012 年，移动广告占 Facebook 广告收入的 14%；到 2018 年已经是 92%。花在手机上的时间序列与它亦步亦趋。

turns.en: Non-voice mobile went from 46 minutes in 2011 to three hours eight minutes in 2016. Today, mobile time for US adults averages four hours per day.
turns.zh: 非通话移动时间从 2011 年的 46 分钟涨到 2016 年的 3 小时 8 分钟。如今，美国成人每天花在移动设备上的时间平均是 4 小时。

turns.en: Clearly, the amount of online information we consume has exploded and the manner in which we ingest media has changed as well. We take in more of it and the nature of it has changed.
turns.zh: 显然，我们消费的在线信息量爆炸式增长，我们吸收媒体的方式也变了。我们摄入得更多，内容的性质也变了。

turns.en: It's not really news as much as content delivered as part of a business model that seeks profit through your engagement. These models are built to maximize attention.
turns.zh: 那些东西与其说是新闻，不如说是一套商业模式交付的内容，而这套模式靠你的参与（engagement）来赚钱。这些模型生来就是为了最大化注意力。

turns.en: That's the objective function rigorously studied and continuously, mathematically fine-tuned. It's powerful and shows little sign of slowing down.
turns.zh: 那就是它的目标函数（objective function）——被严谨地研究，被持续地、数学化地微调。它威力强大，而且丝毫没有减速的迹象。

turns.en: As we voluntarily drown ourselves in content, a new dimension to each story has recently emerged. Odds. Attached to the various situations we follow is now a mapping of probabilities associated with potential outcomes.
turns.zh: 当我们自愿把自己泡在内容里时，每个故事最近又多出一个新的维度：赔率（odds）。如今我们所关注的各种事态，都挂着一张潜在结果对应的概率映射。

turns.en: Will the straight open? Will the Yankees win? Who will take the house? Who shot Tupac? Actually, now we finally know. The advent of Polymarket and Kalshi and DraftKings and FanDuel now give you a real-time window on the probabilities of various resolutions.
turns.zh: 市场会开盘吗？Yankees 会赢吗？谁会拿下众议院？是谁枪杀了 Tupac？其实现在我们终于知道了。Polymarket、Kalshi、DraftKings 和 FanDuel 的出现，给了你一扇实时观察各种结局概率的窗口。

turns.en: They update in real-time. Perhaps not as liquid as Microsoft's stock does, but these engines are discovering new prices for us continuously.
turns.zh: 它们实时更新。流动性也许不如 Microsoft 的股票，但这些引擎在持续不断地为我们发现新的价格。

turns.en: In the process, the prices themselves shape our view on reality. Now, let me go all George Soros on you. No, we're not getting political. We are just risk analysts over here at the Alfa Exchange.
turns.zh: 在这个过程中，价格本身塑造了我们对现实的看法。好了，接下来我要 George Soros 一下了。别紧张，我们不谈政治。在 Alpha Exchange 这边，我们只是风险分析师。

turns.en: When I think of Soros, I am only interested in incorporating some of his powerful reflexivity framework. First, let's all agree that prices surely respond to new information.
turns.zh: 我想起 Soros，感兴趣的只是把他那套强有力的反身性（reflexivity）框架借用过来。首先，我们先都认同一点：价格当然会对新信息做出反应。

turns.en: That's basic stuff. What Soros will say is that as prices respond to changing fundamentals, the new set of prices in turn impacts the fundamentals.
turns.zh: 这是基本功。Soros 的讲法是：当价格对变化的基本面做出反应之后，新一组价格反过来又会影响基本面。

turns.en: In some way, this is a nod to the power of financial conditions, which we will come back to a bit later. I'll add that the prices we engage with continuously shape our view of what the fundamentals actually are.
turns.zh: 在某种意义上，这是向金融条件（financial conditions）的力量致意，这一点我们稍后会再回到。我还要补一句：我们不断打交道的那些价格，也在持续塑造着我们对基本面究竟是什么的看法。

turns.en: Soros is often credited with saying that, quote, price is the only fundamental. This may be in the Mark Twain category of false attribution, but let's just for now pretend Soros said it.
turns.zh: 人们常把“价格是唯一的基本面”这句话安在 Soros 头上。这也许属于 Mark Twain 那一类错误归因，但眼下就先假装是 Soros 说的吧。

turns.en: If price is the only fundamental and prices are increasingly just odds, then our world view is increasingly one in which the odds are the fundamentals.
turns.zh: 如果价格是唯一的基本面，而价格越来越只是赔率，那么我们的世界观就越来越变成：赔率就是基本面。

turns.en: Everything is seen through the prism of odds. The focus on odds is not entirely new. Ask market participants. We are plenty used to deriving ways to allow the market to speak through odds.
turns.zh: 一切都透过赔率的棱镜来看。对赔率的关注并不完全是新鲜事。问问市场参与者就知道，我们早就非常习惯于各种推导，让市场通过赔率开口说话。

turns.en: What are you implying? We might ask Mr. Market. He might respond about what? I can tell you about implied Fed Ikes, about implied defaults, implied correlation, implied dividends, and implied vol to start.
turns.zh: 我们也许会问市场先生（Mr. Market）：你在隐含什么？他可能会反问：关于哪方面？我可以先跟你聊聊隐含加息（implied Fed hikes）、隐含违约、隐含相关性、隐含股息，还有隐含波动率（implied vol）。

turns.en: I imply a lot of things. The point is that we constantly manipulate market prices to back out some sense of expectation. But Kalshi and Polymarket take this to a whole nother level.
turns.zh: 我隐含的东西可不少。要点是，我们不停地利用市场价格反推出某种预期。但 Kalshi 和 Polymarket 把这带到了一个全新的层级。

turns.en: These very neat yes or no bets are easy to understand and, like the over and under on a basketball game, are just binary options. The textbook Arrow Dubro Security is now a real life thing.
turns.zh: 这些干净利落的是/否赌注容易理解，而且就像篮球的大小分盘（over/under）一样，无非是二元期权。教科书里的 Arrow-Debreu 证券，如今成了现实生活的东西。

turns.en: Just a click away on an app that you've attached to yourself every waking minute. And rest easy, you can wage your on Big Brother Season 28's elimination round using it.
turns.zh: 就在你每一刻都贴在身边的那个 App 里，一点就到。放心，用它还能对《Big Brother》第 28 季的淘汰轮下注。

turns.en: As we ingest and internalize not just news but also probabilities, I worry about the U.S. Treasury market becoming headline news for the wrong reasons.
turns.zh: 当我们吸收并内化的不再只是新闻、还有概率的时候，我担心的是，美国国债市场会因为不该有的原因成为头条新闻。

turns.en: Worses said he wants to move the Fed from the front page of the Wall Street Journal. I say that Scott Besen should want the bond market to do the same.
turns.zh: Warsh 说过，他想把美联储从《Wall Street Journal》的头版上挪走。我说，Scott Bessent 也该希望债市同样这么做。

turns.en: Will the U.S. default before 2029 is an actual bet on Kalshi? It's not active to be clear, but it is listed and priced at 11%. Turns out this bet is resolved to yes or no on December 31st, 2028 at 11 p.m.
turns.zh: “美国会在 2029 年前违约吗”，是 Kalshi 上真实存在的一个盘口。说明一下，它并不活跃，但确实挂在上面，定价 11%。原来这个盘要到 2028 年 12 月 31 日晚上 11 点才结算出是或否。

turns.en: I like that, 11 p.m. One can imagine the circumstance if the 31st was actually the day before default and how hectic it might be. That team, a team of glorious leaders seeking to stave off disaster, sitting at the table but not getting there.
turns.zh: 我倒喜欢这个晚上 11 点。可以想象，如果 31 号正好就是违约前一日，那场面会有多紧张。那支“光辉领袖队”想阻止灾难，却坐在谈判桌前谈不拢。

turns.en: Your Kalshi debt default contract doesn't pay. Talk about an unfortunately expiring end of world hedge. But I digress, 11% that is uncomfortably high for me personally.
turns.zh: 你的 Kalshi 债务违约合约就是赔不了。这可真是“恰好在世界末日之前到期”的末日对冲。扯远了。11%——就我个人而言，高得让人不安。

turns.en: Default doesn't sound like a good outcome for us. These prices absolutely become part of how we think about the state of the world. The probabilities become the scorecard.
turns.zh: 违约听起来对我们不是什么好结局。这些价格确实已成为我们思考世界状态的一部分。概率成了记分牌。

turns.en: They almost tell us too much. These incredibly handy probabilities, yes or no is all they speak to, are a new instrument enabling market narratives to become more powerful, shaping our beliefs in the process.
turns.zh: 它们几乎告诉了我们太多。这些无比便捷的概率——它们只会说是或否——是一种新的工具，让市场叙事变得更强大，并在这一过程中塑造着我们的信念。

turns.en: To be sure, the narratives are clearly grounded in some news event. For example, we are not talking about the back end of the US bond market for no reason.
turns.zh: 当然，这些叙事明显植根于某些新闻事件。例如，我们讨论美国债市长端，并非没有来由。

turns.en: What I'm suggesting is that the narrative around it in a world consisting of an endless generation and consumption of content, often with probabilities attached, can reinforce our views and what we believe is objectively true.
turns.zh: 我想说的是，在一个内容被无休止地生产和消费、还常常挂着概率的世界里，围绕事件的叙事会强化我们的观点，以及我们自认为客观为真的东西。

turns.en: Efforts that tie cause and effect underpin most of financial media. Our desire to find the quote why of market moves has always been strong.
turns.zh: 把因果串起来的努力，构成了大半个财经媒体的底色。我们想弄明白市场波动“为什么”的欲望一直非常强烈。

turns.en: And it's difficult not to notice in the FT, Wall Street Journal, Economist and on the Bloomberg Terminal, the focus on the wobbles in the US bond market, how they are driven by frightening deficits and how Besant is determined to quiet any disruption.
turns.zh: 在 FT、《Wall Street Journal》、《Economist》和 Bloomberg 终端上，你很难不注意到大家对美国债市震荡的聚焦：它如何被骇人的赤字驱动，Bessent 如何下定决心平息任何扰动。

turns.en: The FT headline recently quote, Bitcoin and gold surge as Besant's bond market intervention weighs on dollar. Another headline read quote, Besant takes on bond vigilantes in $32 trillion treasure market.
turns.zh: FT 最近的标题是：“Bessent 债市干预打压美元，Bitcoin 和黄金大涨。”另一个标题是：“Bessent 在 32 万亿美元国债市场上迎战债券义警（bond vigilantes）。”

turns.en: In the Wall Street Journal, the headline read how the US went $40 trillion in debt. Continuous exposure to these headlines reinforce how we connect the dots.
turns.zh: 《Wall Street Journal》的标题则是：“美国如何欠下了 40 万亿美元债务。”持续泡在这些标题里，会强化我们连点成线的方式。

turns.en: Check out what I posted on the Alfa exchange recently on Twitter. It's just a series of headlines on US debt. This exercise was really easy to do, just some basic searches.
turns.zh: 可以去看看我最近在 Twitter 上以 Alpha Exchange 名义发的那条，就是一串关于美国债务的标题拼在一起。这个活儿做起来真容易，几下基本搜索就够了。

turns.en: The point is that there is a tremendous amount of attention being paid to US debt, deficits and interest rates. Let's run with this concept of narratives in light of the recent moves in gold and Bitcoin.
turns.zh: 要点在于：美国债务、赤字和利率，正被海量的关注包围。结合 gold 和 Bitcoin 最近的走势，我们顺着叙事这个概念往下走。

turns.en: In markets, there's always an effect in search of a cause. It's the industry just grasping for causality. I especially like the headline that reads quote, S&P up 20 basis points on Iran ceasefire hopes.
turns.zh: 市场里永远有一个结果在寻找一个原因，整个行业都在拼命抓取因果。我特别喜欢这个标题：“S&P 因伊朗停火预期上涨 20 个基点。”

turns.en: Folks, 20 basis points, that's tenuous at best, but we know that financial media is published or perish. There's a story that needs to happen each day.
turns.zh: 各位，20 个基点啊，最多算牵强附会。但我们都懂，财经媒体的法则是“不出版就灭亡”，每天都必须有一个故事发生。

turns.en: But more recently as Besant opened up his front against the bond market, it does appear that gold and Bitcoin have renewed beta to the debasement trade.
turns.zh: 但更近期，随着 Bessent 对债市开辟战线，gold 和 Bitcoin 看起来确实重新获得了对货币贬值交易（debasement trade）的 beta。

turns.en: On August 19th, gold surged by 3% and Bitcoin by 5%. I shared this table on Twitter, but there are only three other instances this has occurred in the past decade.
turns.zh: 8 月 19 日，gold 猛涨 3%，Bitcoin 涨了 5%。我在 Twitter 上分享过这张表：过去十年里这样两者同日大涨的情形，另外只出现过三次。

turns.en: And as Waller made pretty dovish comments on September 3rd, the implied probability of hikes for the September meeting fell and gold and Bitcoin both rose considerably.
turns.zh: 而 Waller 在 9 月 3 日发表了相当鸽派的言论之后，9 月会议加息的隐含概率回落，gold 和 Bitcoin 都大幅上涨。

turns.en: Since Besant's buyback comments, the GLD is up 3% and the IBIT Bitcoin ETF is up 27%. As both assets have rallied sharply in price, their implied vols have risen as well.
turns.zh: 自 Bessent 关于回购的言论以来，GLD 上涨 3%，IBIT 这只 Bitcoin ETF 上涨 27%。随着两类资产价格大涨，它们的隐含波动率也一并上升。

turns.en: This spot up vol up behavior tells us something about the right tail of the distribution and how it's being repriced in these assets. I've covered this extensively on the podcast.
turns.zh: 这种“现货涨、波动率也涨”（spot up, vol up）的行为，反映的是分布右尾（right tail）的情况，以及这些资产的右尾正在被重新定价。这个话题我在播客里讲过很多。

turns.en: These assets are speculative to be sure, but also have disciplined supply, a trait that the treasury market certainly does not at this point.
turns.zh: 这些资产当然是投机性的，但它们的供给有纪律——这一点眼下的国债市场肯定没有。

turns.en: I was flipping channels recently and saw this covered by NBC News. This feels like a narrative that could dominate, becoming self-reinforcing.
turns.zh: 最近我换台，看到 NBC News 也在报道这个。这感觉像一个可能主导局面、并不断自我强化的叙事。

turns.en: We are told the treasury yields are higher because the debt is out of control. And then we get another big increase in the deficit and yields respond to that.
turns.zh: 有人告诉我们，国债收益率更高是因为债务失控。然后我们又看到赤字再来一大块，收益率随即做出反应。

turns.en: It's something to be watchful for. With the unemployment rate at 4.1%, the stock market at an all-time high and GDP growth consistently at 2% or higher, there's just no excuse for the US to run a 6% budget deficit.
turns.zh: 这是要警惕的。失业率 4.1%，股市处在历史新高，GDP 增速始终在 2% 或以上，美国根本没有任何理由还维持着 6% 的预算赤字。

turns.en: This is a structural mismatch between receipts and expenditures. We can argue forever about spending versus taxes. It doesn't really matter.
turns.zh: 这是收入与支出之间的结构性错配。到底是支出还是税收的问题，我们可以永远吵下去，其实没那么重要。

turns.en: The wedge is enormous. We need to think about not just finding more balance, but also from a risk management framework. We have to ask ourselves what could cause receipts to fall and what could cause outlays to rise.
turns.zh: 缺口大得惊人。我们不仅要想怎么找回平衡，更要从风险管理的框架出发问自己：什么会让收入下降？什么会让支出上升？

turns.en: Here let me turn to some thinking I'm doing about two of the country's most substantial assets, our stock market and our bond market. They are our financial twin towers.
turns.zh: 说到这里，我想转到我正在思考的两样东西——这个国家最重要的两项资产：我们的股市和我们的债市。它们是我们的“金融双子塔”。

turns.en: They are attached at the hip. Both assets to each other and threats to each other as well. We need to protect both because either of them faltering poses a significant threat to the other and to the economy at large.
turns.zh: 它们形影不离，既是彼此绑定的资产，也彼此构成威胁。我们必须两个都保护，因为任何一方的失稳，对另一方、对整个经济都是重大威胁。

turns.en: The connection between the stock market, bond market, economic growth and inflation will always be difficult to disentangle. I do think a good case can be made that the wealth effect is a considerably larger than normal component of the strength of today's economy.
turns.zh: 股市、债市、经济增长、通胀之间的联系，永远难以拆解。但我确实认为，可以有理有据地论证：财富效应（wealth effect）在今天经济强劲当中扮演的角色，比常态大得多。

turns.en: Noting that household equity exposure relative to income has more than doubled since 2010, the BIS wrote in June that, quote, a, major equity correction could have a larger macroeconomic consequence today than in the past.
turns.zh: BIS 在 6 月指出，家庭股票敞口相对收入自 2010 年以来已经翻倍不止，并写道：“一场大幅股市回调如今可能比过去造成更大的宏观经济后果。”

turns.en: Former IMF chief economist Gita Gopinath outlined a similar theme in an op-ed written for the economist in October of last year. Her piece was entitled, quote, on the crash that could torch $35 trillion in wealth.
turns.zh: 前 IMF 首席经济学家 Gita Gopinath 在去年 10 月为《Economist》撰写的评论文章里，也阐述了类似的主题。她那篇文章的标题是：《那场可能烧掉 35 万亿美元财富的崩盘》。

turns.en: She points to the notion that a significant sell-off in U.S. equities could spill over into the rest of the world economy as well given foreign ownership of U.S. stocks.
turns.zh: 她指出，鉴于外国对美国股票的持有规模，美股的大幅抛售可能外溢到世界其他地区的经济。

turns.en: Gopinath suggests that a stock market correction on par with the dot-com crash could wipe out $20 trillion of wealth for American households, the equivalent of 70% of GDP in 2024.
turns.zh: Gopinath 估计，一场相当于当年互联网泡沫（dot-com）破裂级别的股市回调，可能抹去美国家庭 20 万亿美元的财富，相当于 2024 年 GDP 的 70%。

turns.en: The consumption aftershocks would be huge, translating to a 2% hit to the overall level of GDP growth. Next, given how invested foreign entities are in the U.S. stock market, she estimates losses for investors outside the U.S. as high as $15 trillion, 20% of the rest of the world's GDP.
turns.zh: 消费的余震会非常巨大，相当于让 GDP 增长的整体水平掉 2 个百分点。其次，考虑到外国主体对美国股市的深度投入，她估计美国以外投资者的损失可能高达 15 万亿美元，相当于世界其他地区 GDP 的 20%。

turns.en: That sure does sound like a lot. AI CapEx has two impacts, one financial and the other economic. On the financial front, it is the driving force for the surge in corporate profitability and share price gains associated with the AI buildout.
turns.zh: 这听起来确实大得吓人。AI 资本开支（CapEx）有两个层面的冲击，一个是金融的，一个是实体的。在金融层面，它就是 AI 建设（AI buildout）所对应的企业盈利激增与股价上涨的驱动力。

turns.en: On the economic front, AI-driven CapEx has become a critical engine spurring U.S. growth. A significant sell-off in these stocks and an associated decline in CapEx could matter through both of these channels at once.
turns.zh: 在经济层面，AI 驱动的 CapEx 已成为拉动美国增长的关键引擎。这些股票一旦遭遇大幅抛售、CapEx 随之回落，这两条渠道会同时发力。

turns.en: The shock to wealth that Gopinath suggests and the BIS points to is the financial impact. The economic impact would be especially significant as well.
turns.zh: Gopinath 所说、BIS 所指的那种财富冲击，是金融层面的影响。经济层面的影响同样会极其重大。

turns.en: Investment in AI data center construction, compute hardware, and networking ran about eight-tenths of U.S. GDP in the first quarter of 2026, pushing computing infrastructure overall to roughly one and a half percent of GDP versus a 2015 to 2022 average of nearly just 70 basis points.
turns.zh: 对 AI 数据中心建设、算力硬件和网络的投资，在 2026 年一季度大约相当于美国 GDP 的 0.8%，把计算基础设施整体推到了约 1.5% 的 GDP 占比——而 2015 到 2022 年的平均只有 70 个基点左右。

turns.en: In the Q1-26 advanced estimate, computer and peripheral equipment investment grew at 67.4% annualized and software at 22.6% annualized, together contributing roughly 1.09 percentage points of the 2% headline growth, against personal consumptions 1.0 percentage points.
turns.zh: 在 2026 年一季度的 advanced estimate（初值）里，计算机及外围设备投资年化增长 67.4%，软件投资年化增长 22.6%，两者合计为 2% 的总量增速贡献了大约 1.09 个百分点，而个人消费贡献了 1.0 个百分点。

turns.en: Neil Dutta of RenMAC made the same observation over a two-quarter window. AI CapEx contributed more to growth than all consumer spending combined.
turns.zh: Renaissance Macro 的 Neil Dutta 在两个季度的窗口上给出了同样的观察：AI CapEx 对增长的贡献，超过了全部消费支出加在一起的总和。

turns.en: In a recent FT op-ed, Bridge Kurana, portfolio manager at Wellington and future Alfa Exchange guest suggests that, quote, high asset prices, not low interest rates, are driving inflation.
turns.zh: 在 FT 最近的一篇评论文章里，Wellington 的组合经理、未来的 Alpha Exchange 嘉宾 Bridge Kurana 提出：“推高通胀的是高资产价格，而不是低利率。”

turns.en: Bridge argues that in order to tame inflation, worse needs to slow the growth in asset prices, largely a function of credit-driven expansion in the AI realm of the economy.
turns.zh: Kurana 认为，要驯服通胀，Warsh 就得让资产价格的增速慢下来——而后者在很大程度上是经济里 AI 这个领域信用驱动扩张的一个函数。

turns.en: Let's turn there next because that could be very tricky. In his first press conference, war suggested that financial conditions are restrictive in some areas of the economy like housing.
turns.zh: 接下来我们就聊这个，因为这可能非常棘手。在第一次记者会上，Warsh 就表示，金融条件在经济的一些领域——比如房地产——是偏紧的。

turns.en: That's hard to argue with as 30-year mortgage rates approach 7% again. But if the dominant component of the economy is AI-centric CapEx funded by hyperscalers issuing debt, it would seem not restrictive enough, at least based on the flood of issuance now and plan for 2027 and beyond.
turns.zh: 当 30 年期房贷利率再次逼近 7% 的时候，这话很难反驳。但如果经济的主导部分是围绕 AI 的 CapEx、由 hyperscalers（超大规模云厂商）发债融资，那金融条件看起来又还不够紧——至少从目前发行量的洪峰和 2027 年及以后的计划来看是这样。

turns.en: Unlike the U.S. government, these companies are using the debt to seek profit. The right tail of riches sought via the AI trade should be thought of in an option framework.
turns.zh: 与美国政府不同，这些公司举债是为了寻求利润。通过 AI 交易去追逐的那条“富贵的右尾”，应该放在期权框架里来思考。

turns.en: The cost of debt is option premium that is likely too low. Merton's framework values a corporate bond spread as optionality. The buyer is paid the premium to absorb default risk.
turns.zh: 债务成本就是一笔期权权利金，而且很可能太低了。Merton 的框架把公司债利差（spread）估值成一种期权性：买方收取权利金，来吸收违约风险。

turns.en: The issuer pays the spread, which is compensation for the option the buyer sold to it. In this context, it's worth considering that hyperscalers are not solving for coupon.
turns.zh: 发行人支付利差，作为对买方卖给它的期权的补偿。在这个语境下，值得琢磨的一点是：hyperscalers 求解的并不是票息。

turns.en: They're buying cheap optionality on a TAM they believe is enormous. The hyperscalers could be pretty price inelastic given the value they assign to right tail outcomes.
turns.zh: 他们是在用便宜的权利金，买一个他们相信无比庞大的 TAM（潜在市场总量）上的期权性。考虑到他们赋予右尾结果的价值，hyperscalers 在价格上很可能相当不敏感（price inelastic）。

turns.en: The U.S. government is also price inelastic, but for a very different reason, giant structural deficits that require an endless new supply of bonds, even just to pay interest on the existing debt.
turns.zh: 美国政府在价格上同样不敏感，但原因完全不同：庞大的结构性赤字要求源源不断的新债供给——哪怕只是为了支付现有债务的利息。

turns.en: The old notion is that government borrowing can crowd out the private sector and raise the cost of its capital. Some are suggesting the reverse may be true today.
turns.zh: 老观点认为，政府借款会挤出私营部门、抬高它的资本成本。有人提出，今天反过来的情形可能才是真的。

turns.en: I think that framing is worth considering. Fund for capital to fund the AI build out may simply require higher base treasury yields. That could be very tricky at a time when the narrative has become more skeptical on U.S.
turns.zh: 我觉得这个提法值得考虑：为 AI 建设提供资金，可能本就需要更高的基准国债收益率。在叙事对美国财政已经变得更加怀疑的当下，这会非常棘手。

turns.en: fiscal issues. Thus, the quote binding constraints on the AI build out most commonly cited are some combination of power, infrastructure, memory, and data center resistance.
turns.zh: 因此，人们最常引用的 AI 建设的“紧约束”（binding constraints），是电力、基础设施、存储（memory）和数据中心阻力的某种组合。

turns.en: Maybe however, it's just capital. Not much can work if the risk-free market doesn't. Where Fed policy gets extremely fraught is that if slowing the economy down to TAM inflation amounts to slowing CAPX and potentially causing a decided sell-off in the stock market in the process, that in turn could feedback sharply into the economy via the wealth effect.
turns.zh: 但也许，约束就是资本本身。如果无风险市场转不动，很多事都转不动。美联储政策之所以极其凶险，在于：如果为了驯服通胀而让经济降温，等于给 CapEx 踩刹车，并可能在这个过程中引发股市一轮明显的抛售——而那又会通过财富效应剧烈地反噬经济。

turns.en: The speed and extent to which monetary policy transmits to the real economy is always uncertain. Let's quickly talk about Stanley Druckenmiller's and Claude's, I suppose, Wall Street Journal op-ed, shall we?
turns.zh: 货币政策传导到实体经济的速度和程度，从来都是不确定的。我们赶紧聊聊 Stanley Druckenmiller 和 Claude（联手写的那篇）《Wall Street Journal》评论文章吧，怎么样？

turns.en: To be sure, the Twitter was on fire in the days that followed the August 24th Wall Street Journal op-ed piece entitled, quote, Let the Bond Market Speak.
turns.zh: 确实，8 月 24 日那篇题为《Let the Bond Market Speak》（让债市说话）的《Wall Street Journal》评论文章刊发之后的几天里，Twitter 上吵翻了天。

turns.en: But mostly around whether it was okay if it was written by AI. There are lots of views here, some nuanced. Even the Wall Street Journal defended the piece and the nondisclosure of Claude's work.
turns.zh: 但争论主要集中在“由 AI 执笔到底行不行”。这个问题上观点很多，也有一些很细腻。连《Wall Street Journal》自己都站出来为这篇文章、为没有披露 Claude 的参与进行辩护。

turns.en: Druck says he was, quote, kind of proud of using it, referencing the help of AI. Weeks earlier, the Financial Times had taken a very different stance with a maya culpa on work that AI had helped generate.
turns.zh: Druck 说他对自己使用 AI 这件事“有点引以为豪”。而几周前，《Financial Times》采取了截然不同的姿态，就 AI 参与生产的内容刊发了一篇 mea culpa（忏悔认错文）。

turns.en: To me, this is a really interesting topic. When we calculate a regression statistic, we do not disclose that we haven't properly inverted a matrix by hand to do so.
turns.zh: 对我来说，这是一个非常有意思的话题。我们计算一个回归统计量的时候，并不会披露“自己其实没有手工正确地求逆过矩阵”。

turns.en: Sure, but this is writing and it's on a critical topic from a very important person. If Druck disclosed that AI wrote this, no one would have read it the same way.
turns.zh: 是啊，但这可是写作，而且是一位极重要人物谈一个关键议题。如果 Druck 披露这是 AI 写的，没有人会用同样的眼光去读它。

turns.en: I'm personally a big fan of writing. I love reading Jim Grant, not because I think Jim is always right, but because his writing style is unique and because as I'm reading the words, I can hear Jim's voice.
turns.zh: 我个人非常热爱好的写作。我爱读 Jim Grant 的文字，不是因为我觉得 Jim 永远正确，而是因为他的文风独一无二——读着这些字句，我能听见 Jim 的声音。

turns.en: The disclose or not debate overwhelmed the real story. One of the most respected macro hedge fund managers in history delivered a scorching rebuke of U.S. fiscal dynamics and a strong warning for what could be coming.
turns.zh: 而“披露与否”的争论，淹没了真正的重点。历史上最受尊敬的宏观对冲基金经理之一，对美国财政动态给出一通激烈的痛斥，并对可能到来的风险发出了强烈警告。

turns.en: The numbers aren't possible to deny. No matter if Druck wrote it or not, it's a thumbs down on Besson's recent actions and the notion that one can suppress the market's truth-telling efforts.
turns.zh: 那些数字不容否认。不管是不是 Druck 亲笔，这都是给 Bessent 近期的举动、以及那种以为可以压制市场讲真话的想法，打了一个倒彩。

turns.en: Fiscal discipline must return, Druck says, through entitlement reform. There is no easy way, but the hardest way is through some awful surge in long-dated bond yields in which the vigilantes strike back.
turns.zh: Druck 说，财政纪律必须回归，途径是 entitlement reform（法定福利支出改革）。没有轻松的路，而最难的那条，是长期限债券收益率某种可怕的飙升——债券义警们卷土重来。

turns.en: Fiscal dynamics being what they are, the Treasury Secretary should be a market stabilizer. Today, Besson is a source of all. He's all in on fights with Elizabeth Warren, Canada, Iran, and more recently, the global bond market.
turns.zh: 就目前的财政态势而言，财政部长本应是市场的稳定器。而今天的 Bessent 却是一切动荡的源头。他全力以赴地投入与 Elizabeth Warren、与加拿大、与伊朗的争斗，最近又加上了全球债市。

turns.en: He was dismissive of Druck and Claude's op-ed. Druck and Miller's piece was a valuable warning for Besson. Instead of treating it that way, Besson said, quote, stands a great investor.
turns.zh: 他对 Druck 和 Claude 的那篇评论很是不屑。对 Bessent 来说，Druck 这篇文章本是一份宝贵的警示。可 Bessent 不这么对待它，他说：“可真是位伟大的投资人。”

turns.en: He changes his mind a lot and he doesn't like losing money. I think he lost money the day he sent in the editorial. What an oddly specific comment on a one-day mark-to-market outcome for a private investor coming from the Treasury Secretary.
turns.zh: “他主意改得特别快，而且不喜欢亏钱。我看他投出这篇稿的那天就亏钱了。”财政部长对一个私人投资者一天的盯市（mark-to-market）结果，说出这么古怪又具体的评论。

turns.en: This is unearned bravado at a time when both humility and leadership are critical right now. Besson is currently showing neither. This is a new risk factor we haven't seen before, a disrespect for market prices and the signals they send.
turns.zh: 这是一种没来由的虚张声势——眼下，谦逊和领导力都至关重要，而 Bessent 目前两样都没表现出来。这是一个我们以前没见过的风险因素：对市场价格及其发出信号的轻慢。

turns.en: The global risk-free market, of which the US is by far the largest, is a front-page story right now. Effective communication from the Treasury Secretary is going to become increasingly important.
turns.zh: 全球最大的无风险市场——美国部分是遥遥领先的——如今正是头版故事。财政部长沟通的有效性，会越来越重要。

turns.en: Besson seems to embrace his role of hedge fund manager with a pretty large capacity to bear risk. To borrow from the movie Loan Survivor, Scott Besson is fixing for a pretty good gunfight.
turns.zh: Bessent 似乎很享受对冲基金经理这个角色，带着相当大的风险承受能力。借用电影《Lone Survivor》的话说，Scott Bessent 这是正巴不得来一场痛快的枪战。

turns.en: Let's hope it all works out. To bring all of this discussion thus far together, the fourth type of risk off is a US Treasury motivated vol episode that isn't primarily about monetary policy tightening.
turns.zh: 但愿一切都能有好结果。把我们到目前为止的讨论合起来看：第四种避险，是一次由美国国债驱动的波动率（vol）行情，而且主要不是因为货币政策收紧。

turns.en: It's a confidence thing. If policymakers aren't already gaming out potential scenarios on this, we are in trouble. I'm not at all saying this will happen, but risk management is about planning.
turns.zh: 这是一个信心的问题。如果政策制定者还没有推演过这背后的各种情景，那我们就有麻烦了。我完全不是说这一定会发生，但风险管理讲的就是未雨绸缪。

turns.en: Let me leave you with some thoughts on a date, a season, the overall climate, and ultimately some views on the price of insurance. First the date, the FOMC meeting coming on September 16th.
turns.zh: 最后留给大家几点思考：一个日子、一个季节、整体的气候，以及最终关于保险价格的一些看法。先说日子——9 月 16 日即将召开的 FOMC 会议。

turns.en: I personally remain struck at the lack of risk premium between TLT options that expire just before the September 16th meeting and just after it.
turns.zh: 就我个人而言，我一直对这一点感到吃惊：恰好在 9 月 16 日会议前到期、与恰好在会议后到期的 TLT 期权之间，几乎没有风险溢价。

turns.en: I like buying a calendar spread that isolates the movements in the TLT coming from the Worst Press Conference on September 16th. Next a season.
turns.zh: 我喜欢做一个日历价差（calendar spread），把 TLT 因 9 月 16 日 Warsh 记者会而产生的波动单独隔离出来。接下来是一个季节。

turns.en: I've been asking myself recently, is there seasonality in S&P vol? I'm not personally convinced yet that there is, but I am convinced that others are convinced there is, and that may be all that is needed.
turns.zh: 我最近一直在问自己：S&P 的波动率有季节性吗？我个人还没被说服，但我确信“别人确信有”，而这也许就是所需要的全部。

turns.en: Risks do tend to sharpen their pencils as back to school approaches, and October is historically the most volatile month of the year. Since 1996, 40% of the October's has seen a realized vol north of 20%.
turns.zh: 随着开学季临近，做风险的人确实往往会“削尖铅笔”，而 10 月在历史上是一年中最波动的月份。自 1996 年以来，40% 的 10 月里，已实现波动率都在 20% 以上。

turns.en: It's the most consistently volatile month. I presented a chart on this on Twitter. I like setting up hedges with October expiration. And what about the overall climate for risk?
turns.zh: 它是波动最稳定的一个月份。我喜欢布置 10 月到期的对冲。那么，风险的整体气候如何？

turns.en: I've argued that low correlation is osempic for portfolio volatility. Enjoy the results, I guess, but beware the side effects of off-label use.
turns.zh: 我说过，低相关性之于组合波动率，就像 Olympic（奥运级兴奋剂）一样的存在。要享受成果可以，但小心 off-label（超适应症）使用的副作用。

turns.en: The TLDR on this is that ultra low correlations are over diversifying portfolios, reducing risk in an unsustainable way. Do not trust them or rely on them.
turns.zh: 这件事的 TLDR 是：超低的相关性正在让组合过度分散化，以一种不可持续的方式压低风险。不要相信它们，也不要依赖它们。

turns.en: These correlations could shift in an instant. S&P realized vol over the last month is 8.6, not much to see here at all. But beneath the surface, huge daily motion in the single names.
turns.zh: 这些相关性可能瞬息生变。过去一个月 S&P 的已实现波动率是 8.6，简直没什么可看的。但水面之下，个股的日内波动大得惊人。

turns.en: The average one-month realized vol of the top 10 names in the S&P is 46. It's a spread that recently reached 40 vol points. Blame faltering correlation, which is leaving volatility starved at the index level.
turns.zh: S&P 市值前 10 名个股的一个月已实现波动率平均值是 46，两者之间的裂口最近达到了 40 个波动点。要怪就怪摇摇欲坠的相关性——它让指数层面的波动率严重“吃不饱”。

turns.en: My penchant for looking around corners is to warn that leaning in to realized volatility to size a portfolio is risky because of how depressed realized is due this low correlation.
turns.zh: 我这种喜欢绕到拐角往前看的癖好，让我给出一个警告：靠已实现波动率来定组合仓位是有风险的，因为低相关性已经把已实现波动率压得如此萎靡。

turns.en: The speed with which that could correct would jolt index vol higher. As I said, do not trust or rely on these low correlations. My take on this is simple.
turns.zh: 而它一旦修正，那个速度会把指数波动率猛地拽上去。我说过：不要相信、不要依赖这些低相关性。我的看法很简单。

turns.en: Investors must be careful not to bank these never seen before levels of diversification across stocks and the resulting reduction in realized vol at the portfolio level.
turns.zh: 投资者必须小心，不要把股票之间前所未见的分散化水平，以及由此带来的组合层面已实现波动率的下降，当成可以存进银行的资本。

turns.en: It's dangerous because you may wind up largely mis-sizing once the inevitable correlation spike does occur. If realized correlation on the stock-to-stock front is unsustainably low and stock bond correlation is high and unreliable, where do you turn for risk management?
turns.zh: 这很危险，因为一旦那场 inevitable 的相关性飙升真的发生，你最后很可能发现仓位大小完全错了。如果个股之间的已实现相关性低得不可持续，股债相关性又高又靠不住，风险管理还能转向哪里？

turns.en: Risk-based risk reduction is incredibly affordable and I would argue too low relative to the overall set of uncertainties in the macro climate.
turns.zh: 基于风险工具的风险削减（risk-based risk reduction）便宜得难以置信——我认为，相对宏观气候里那一整套不确定性而言，它低得不正常。

turns.en: I posted this on Twitter a few times, an index I created of cross-asset vol percentiles. It is the average of five-year percentiles of the VIX, VIX-TLT, CVIX, high-yield credit spreads and credit-implied vol.
turns.zh: 这个东西我在 Twitter 上发过好几次：我自建的一个跨资产波动率分位数指数。它取 VIX、VIX-TLT、CVIX、高收益信用利差、信用隐含波动率这五个指标 5 年分位数的平均值。

turns.en: It recently was below the 10th percentile. Said a little differently, health insurance costs way too much, but wealth insurance costs way too little.
turns.zh: 它最近低于第 10 百分位。换一种说法：健康保险贵得离谱，而财富保险便宜得离谱。

turns.en: The biggest risk management question for investors is around whether these large tech companies massively uncorrelated when it comes to daily returns but in the same business will turn out to exhibit much more co-movement than is currently priced.
turns.zh: 对投资者来说，最大的风险管理问题是：这些大型科技公司，日常回报的相关性极低、做的却是同一门生意——它们最终会不会表现出远比当前定价更强的共同运动（co-movement）？

turns.en: The answer in my view is most certainly yes and that's simply because the market nearly disregards completely the potential for a correlation event.
turns.zh: 我的看法是，答案几乎必然是“会”，原因很简单：市场几乎完全无视了一次相关性事件（correlation event）发生的可能。

turns.en: That's why the VIX and short-dated VIX futures sit in exceedingly low percentiles. One month realized correlation on the S&P is, wait for it, one percent.
turns.zh: 这就是 VIX 和短期限 VIX 期货停在极低分位数的原因。S&P 一个月已实现相关性是多少？你听好了——1%。

turns.en: For three months, it's four percent. We've never seen anything like this before. What is causing it? I cannot definitively say, but what it causes, I certainly do know, depressed index volatility and a vulnerability called over extrapolation.
turns.zh: 三个月的是 4%。我们从来没见过这样的东西。是什么造成的？我给不出定论，但它造成什么，我确实知道：被压抑的指数波动率，和一个叫“过度外推（over extrapolation）”的脆弱点。

turns.en: We assume that the low correlation of today, last week and last month, will continue going forward. These assumptions get baked into market prices.
turns.zh: 我们假设今天、上周、上个月那种低相关性会一直延续下去。这些假设被烤进了市场价格里。

turns.en: My increasingly strong view is that these option prices as represented by metrics like the VIX, while fair to realize, are highly out of step with the vast level of uncertainty in the world, in policy and in markets, part with some option premium and by vol, I say.
turns.zh: 我越来越强烈的观点是：这些期权价格——以 VIX 这类指标为代表——相对已实现波动虽然算公允，却与世界、政策、市场中巨大的不确定性水平严重脱节。我说，掏一点期权权利金，买点波动率吧。

turns.en: Implied vol can be forward looking when there's a date certain event on the calendar that can catalyze a move. Think earnings, FOMC, CPI, elections.
turns.zh: 当日历上有一个日期确定、能够催化行情的事情时，隐含波动率可以是有前瞻性的。想想财报、FOMC、CPI、选举。

turns.en: But for the most part, implied is dictated by realized vol. And for each of the assets I mentioned above, that's keeping a lid on implied volatility.
turns.zh: 但多数情况下，隐含是由已实现波动率说了算。对我上面提到的每一种资产，这都压制着隐含波动率。

turns.en: It's very difficult to call the low involved, and it's very easy to postpone buying options when the index is realizing so little, especially on down days.
turns.zh: 给低波动率择时非常困难，而当指数实现的波动如此之小——尤其是在下跌的日子里——推迟买入期权就变得太容易了。

turns.en: If we calculate realized vol on the subset of down days, only over the past month, it's just seven point eight percent. That does little to motivate hedging.
turns.zh: 如果只在过去一个月下跌的那些交易日里计算已实现波动率，只有 7.8%。这几乎给不了人对冲的动力。

turns.en: You don't want to miss snagging protection at low levels, but being early can leave you putting out premium that doesn't stand the test of time.
turns.zh: 你不想错过在低位抓到便宜保护的机会，但出手太早，可能让你交出去的权利金经不起时间的考验。

turns.en: If markets can stay irrational longer than you can stay solvent as the saying goes, then markets can also stay quiet longer than you can stay patient with the hedging program.
turns.zh: 俗话说，市场保持非理性的时间可能比你能保持偿付能力的时间更长；那么同样，市场保持沉寂的时间，也可能比你对一套对冲计划保持耐心的时间更长。

turns.en: At these levels of index vol, it's really worth starting to pick away. volatility and vol may not really be a thing, but enough good folks believe in it such that a Pavlovian buying of vol around this time creates a floor and a bid.
turns.zh: 在这样的指数波动率水平上，真的值得开始一点点分批布局了。季节性、波动率也许并不真是什么“东西”，但有足够多的好人相信它，以至于在这个时节对波动率那种巴甫洛夫式的买入，就会造出一个底部和一个买盘。

turns.en: September VIX futures expire the morning of a critical FOMC. There's plenty of scope for one month S&P options, which the VIX futures expire to, to embed some risk premium for that meeting.
turns.zh: 9 月的 VIX 期货恰好在关键的 FOMC 当天上午到期。VIX 期货所锚定的那一个月期 S&P 期权，完全有空间为那次会议嵌入一些风险溢价。

turns.en: There's a great scene in the big short where Ryan Gosling played playing Greg Lipman tells Jeremy Strong playing Steve Isman's Trader Vinnie Daniel quote sharpen your pencils.
turns.zh: 《The Big Short》里有一场精彩的戏：Ryan Gosling 演的 Greg Lippmann 对 Jeremy Strong 演的 Steve Eisman 手下那位叫 Vinnie Daniel 的交易员说：“把你们的铅笔削尖了。”

turns.en: I'll get the paperwork ready as front point is set to put on their first CDS trades to get short housing. My contention is that traders and equity vol are also set to sharpen their pencils as vol drifts lower and the inevitable quiet of the last week before Labor Day has imposed itself on the cost of carry.
turns.zh: “我这就去把文书准备好。”——那是他们即将建立第一笔做空房地产的 CDS 交易之时。我的论点是：当波动率走低、Labor Day 前最后一周那种必然的沉寂已经压低了持有成本（cost of carry），股票波动率的交易者们也在削尖他们的铅笔。

turns.en: There is going to start to be demand for volatility. Perhaps it's folks like me shouting from the rooftops. Perhaps it's the idea that there is seasonality of vol which shows up as elevated in September and October and induces folks to front run the expected pickup before others do to repeat prices in options have come your way.
turns.zh: 对波动率的需求将会开始起来。也许是因为有我这样在屋顶上呐喊的人；也许是因为“波动率有季节性、会在 9 月和 10 月走高”这个念头，驱使人们抢在他人之前抢跑这轮预期的抬升——期权里的重新定价总会向你走来。

turns.en: But don't be too patient and seeking the low average in these are fantastic prices. They are nominally very low and set against the multiple sources of potential disruption cheap to the actual risks in the world.
turns.zh: 但也别太执着于抄那个“低位均价”——这些实在是极好的价格。它们名义上非常低，而对照潜在的多个扰动源，相对于世界里真实存在的风险，它们便宜得很。

turns.en: I hope you have found this discussion valuable. I've wanted to communicate a few chief ideas first to lay out the fourth risk off an episode that features instability in the back end of the U.S. bond market.
turns.zh: 我希望这期讨论对你有价值。我本想传达几个主要想法。第一，把第四种避险讲清楚——一次以美国债市长端不稳为特征的事件。

turns.en: As I've said, nothing can really work in markets if the Treasury market does not count me is worried that the U.S. fiscal issues are incredibly difficult to solve.
turns.zh: 正如我说的，如果国债市场转不动，市场里什么都行不通。让我担心的是，美国的财政问题极其难解。

turns.en: We wouldn't be here otherwise and that the timeline to address them has shortened. We live in a world of hyper generated narratives. I've argued that the U.S. economy and market are far too exposed to the AI capex trade.
turns.zh: 否则我们不会落到这一步——而且解决它们的时间表已经缩短。我们生活在一个叙事被过度生产的世界里。我说过，美国经济和市场在 AI CapEx 交易上的暴露实在太高了。

turns.en: There are various correlations that emerge between the companies in the value chain between the economy and the market. But the correlations are extremely unpriced and that means derivatives are nominally quite cheap because index volatility is so low.
turns.zh: 价值链上的公司之间、经济与市场之间，正在形成各种各样的相关性。但这些相关性在定价中极度缺位，这意味着衍生品名义上相当便宜，因为指数波动率如此之低。

turns.en: The AI build out is demanding capital that is likely putting upward pressure on real rates. A prospective home buyer may certainly find a 7% mortgage rate restrictive.
turns.zh: AI 建设正在索取资本，这很可能在给实际利率带来向上的压力。一个准备买房的人，当然会觉得 7% 的房贷利率是紧的。

turns.en: A hyperscaler chasing AI gold may not find the current cost of debt capital restrictive at all. If getting inflation to target means slowing this capex materially leading to a meaningful decline in the equity market, there could be substantial knock on impacts via the wealth effect and an economy which has gathered so much beta to ongoing capex.
turns.zh: 但一个追逐 AI 淘金热的 hyperscaler，可能根本不觉得当前的债务资金成本有约束。如果要把通胀带回目标就必须显著拉慢 CapEx、并导致股市一轮有意义的下跌，那么经由财富效应、经由一个已经对持续 CapEx 积聚了大量 beta 的经济，连锁冲击可能相当可观。

turns.en: So there are two correlations worth worrying about. First among the stocks. Because realized correlation is so low the S&P 500 moves very little.
turns.zh: 所以有两个相关性值得担心。第一个是股票之间的。因为已实现相关性如此之低，S&P 500 几乎不怎么动。

turns.en: That means that traders can't pay much for options because realized vol at the index level is so low and won't allow them to. They just don't carry well these options at higher prices.
turns.zh: 这意味着交易者没法为期权付太多钱，因为指数层面的已实现波动率太低、由不得他们。这些期权以更高的价格拿着，根本 carry 不动。

turns.en: My view is that forward realized correlation could be substantially higher than the levels we are enjoying right now. That could lead to a shock higher to index volatility and more broadly the connection between these tech behemoths and the US economy.
turns.zh: 我的观点是，前瞻的已实现相关性可能大幅高于我们此刻正在“享受”的水平。那可能导致指数波动率的一次冲击式上跳；更广义地说，还有这些科技巨头与美国经济之间联系的重估。

turns.en: There's an old saying that the economy does not equal the market. Actually these days it absolutely does. The same stocks responsible for equity market wealth are also responsible for generating economic growth.
turns.zh: 老话说，经济不等于市场。其实如今两者完全划上了等号。为股市创造财富的那同一批股票，也正是拉动经济增长的那批股票。

turns.en: This is another uncomfortable and I'd argue underappreciated correlation. Buckle up. The midterms are coming. Monetary policy is in flux. The back end of the yield curve is wobbling.
turns.zh: 这是又一个令人不安、而且我认为被低估的相关性。系好安全带吧。中期选举在逼近，货币政策在动荡，收益率曲线的长端在摇晃。

turns.en: The AI trade is way too concentrated. And vol is at levels we don't often see. If you haven't noticed I like spending some money on insurance.
turns.zh: AI 交易集中的程度实在太过分。而波动率在我们不常见到的低水平。如果你已经注意到了——我就是个喜欢花钱买保险的人。
